Original nodes remain selectable. Generated names use B ⇐ A · suffix. Only known top-level intermediaries are used; nested selectors and remote providers are not expanded. Existing non-DIRECT chains are skipped. Changes require a restart when running and never start the VPN automatically. Generation does not prove connectivity.

Apply OR, then AND, then exclusions. Full-width ｜ ＆ ！ work like | & !. Ignore case and whitespace around each term, including full-width spaces; internal spaces are literal. No parentheses or regex. Selector filters still apply. Missing matches produce diagnostics, never placeholder nodes.

Target filters match final selector names; intermediary filters match A within each selector. An empty target filter uses the selector named by the first top-level MATCH/FINAL. URL landing filters only select imported B nodes.
hk | jp & gm & !ev equals hk & gm & !ev | jp: contain hk or jp, also contain gm, and exclude ev. Empty intermediary or landing filters match all names.

Do not mix URI and YAML or multiple YAML documents. Source rules, selectors and listeners are omitted; existing dialer-proxy is replaced by group composition. Bad URI nodes are skipped with reasons; invalid shared DNS/certificate metadata rejects the input. Chain composition does not rewrite subscription sources; credentials stay in private app storage.
Import URI, Base64 URI or mihomo YAML nodes in bulk. Paste one object, an array or a proxies list. Editing a node retains its DNS/hosts dependencies.
Maintain landing protocol, authentication, TLS and transport fields manually. URI parameters share the subscription parser; arrays and objects use encoded JSON.
Manage landing nodes B and associate groups with subscriptions. Match intermediaries A in final selectors and append copies for Device → A → B → target.
Paste self-hosted exits into manual groups or manage URLs in subscription groups. Groups can be shared across subscriptions independently of local configuration or script associations.

Only adding, editing or manual refresh accesses the network. Lists hide full URLs; reveal them explicitly in the editor. Leaving or backgrounding cancels requests. Sources commit independently; failures keep old nodes and cancellation keeps completed updates. Size, redirect and time limits apply. Reopen stale editors instead of overwriting newer revisions.
Fetch landing nodes from HTTP/HTTPS sources with independent name filters. Keep each source’s last successful nodes, timestamp and conversion report.
Keep multiple URLs in a group and refresh one source, one group or all sources. A valid source may be saved even when its filter currently matches no nodes.

The source is unchanged and source routing is omitted. Unrecognized or malformed URI nodes are skipped with reasons. No usable nodes, invalid shared DNS/certificate metadata or failed final validation preserve the previous subscription. Parsing does not verify connectivity; Home DNS overrides still apply as configured.

Detect Surge, plain URI, or Base64 URI subscriptions. URIs use mihomo proxy field names and encoded JSON for arrays and objects, while retaining existing aliases. Convert nodes and DNS before applying the linked local configuration or script and Home runtime settings.
Import subscriptions from other clients or inspect missing nodes, certificate pins and DNS conversion results.
